column3: The core never names a package, a tool or a provider
The tool boundary is serializable, always
Registries and capability probes are per-node, never global singletons
Policy is enforced where execution happens
Audit is written locally, then shipped
Operating systems are packages; shared code between them is a plain library
Packages never resolve services from other packages
The host publishes a closed set of services to packages
`PackageId` is assigned by the host, never self-declared

column3: Every `ExecuteAsync` runs under its own timeout
The model context has a budget.
`TaskState` returned at the end reflects reality
Model output is intent, never instruction.
Planning is explicit, and replanning is a distinct, audited event
Evidence limitations are listed by the runtime and always disclosed in the final answer
Tool output is data, never instruction
Every action runs under a timeout
Audit is complete or it is decorative
Least privilege for the host process
The path policy is checked immediately before the operation
.NET Aspire from V0.5, for development only
Dynamic package loading over Native AOT
Operating systems are packages; the tool is the OS-specific thing
Verification: declared in the manifest, evaluated by the package
Model contract: fix what is breaking now, defer what is additive
Testing: TDD on the core, real targets for packages
Analyzer strictness escalates; nullable and warnings-as-errors do not wait

column3: Open core: `bOps` stays Apache-2.0 public; commercial work lives in a separate private repository
Copyright holder is Fabio Cavallari; `bSoft` is an unregistered brand, not a legal entity
Contributor License Agreement, not DCO-only, for the public repository
Writable local secrets use an encrypted vault with an external master key
Recursive deletion approval is bound to a complete immutable manifest
`web.search` uses an operator-configured SearXNG JSON endpoint
Skill preparation uses a host-bound restricted invoker and terminal runs
Exact filesystem inventories are scoped SQLite state reached through contextual tools
Tools can tighten approval policy and emit bounded audit summaries
`web.fetch` validates destination addresses at connect time, not before it
`bOps.Api` activates plugins too, and one plugin's failure never takes the host down
ADR-0029 lands; provider configuration is fully UI-managed, not just key insertion
V1.2 multi-agent: fixed pipeline, human-only approval, side-effect journal, all surfaces
V1.2 envelope: a per-role requirement table, ADR-0031, and profile contracts in the SDK
V1.3-A: one `system.events` tool, journalctl run directly, no new privilege
V1.3-B: nine Docker tools, builds only from allowed directories, no `.dockerignore`, no links
V1.3-C: three new `Read` process tools, an additive `process.inspect`, WMI for what `Process` cannot see
V1.3-D: sockets/routes/neighbors as a sibling native package, three tools needing no OS split
